issue.title: Recover stuck preparing drafts and skip companies with an open draft in auto-prepare
issue.body:
## Overview

An unattended `npm run auto-prepare` run that gets killed mid-draft (log-off,
shutdown, Task Scheduler stopping the process) leaves that application stuck
in `preparing` (the state a job sits in while its resume and cover letter are
being tailored) forever. Nothing ever moves it out, and it silently counts
toward the "queue full" limit, so enough stuck rows make every later run
report `queue-full` and exit `0` — the feature stops producing new drafts with
no error anywhere. Separately, the same-company de-duplication that is meant
to stop a second draft going out for a company that already has one waiting
only works within a single run, so a company with a draft still sitting in
`preparing` or `review` from an earlier run can get a second one today.

**Engineering refinement was skipped for this issue.** Both fixes are
localized to one service and one repository query, the cause was identified
during the PR #12 QA review by reading the code (not guessed), and neither
changes an assisted-apply guardrail.

## User story

As the owner, I want a run that got interrupted to clean up after itself, so
that unattended preparation keeps producing new drafts run after run instead
of quietly going stale, and so that I never end up with two drafts open for
the same company.

## Context

- Source: QA review on merged PR #12, non-blocking suggestions 2 and 3
  (https://github.com/anthonyturner/jobpilot/pull/12#issuecomment-5814526313).
- Parent: #8.
- [countWaitingForReview](server/src/persistence/application-repository.ts#L79-L81)
  counts every application in `preparing` or `review`, with no limit on how
  long a row has been `preparing`.
- [AutoPrepareService.run](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L57-L84)
  computes how much room is left in the review queue from that count before
  selecting any candidates, and stops immediately with outcome `queue-full`
  once it hits zero. A killed process leaves its in-progress application in
  `preparing` — nothing in the codebase ever moves a `preparing` row anywhere
  else.
- The PR #12 QA review's own evidence puts one draft at up to ~8 minutes; a
  30-minute staleness threshold (how old a `preparing` row has to be before
  it's treated as abandoned rather than in progress) leaves a wide margin
  against a slow-but-live draft.
- There is an existing, working precedent for exactly this shape of recovery,
  for sweep (job search) runs rather than applications:
  [RunRepository.markInterrupted](server/src/persistence/run-repository.ts#L59-L63)
  marks any run left `running` as `interrupted`.
  [composition.ts](server/src/composition.ts#L32-L35) only calls it for the
  server (`recoverInterruptedRuns` defaults to `true`; see the call at
  [composition.ts#L128](server/src/composition.ts#L128)) — the CLI entry
  points ([prepare-once.ts](server/src/cli/prepare-once.ts#L17),
  `sync-once.ts`) explicitly pass `false`, because a command-line process can
  start while the server is mid-sweep and must not mark that sweep
  interrupted. The same server-vs-CLI distinction likely applies to
  recovering `preparing` applications.
- `AuditActor` is `'user' | 'scheduler' | 'ingest' | 'agent'`
  ([audit-repository.ts#L3](server/src/persistence/audit-repository.ts#L3));
  `'scheduler'` is already the actor `AutoPrepareService` uses for its own
  `autoprepare.*` events, so it is a non-user actor already in use for this
  exact flow.
- Separately,
  [AutoPrepareService.skipReason](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L110-L120)
  only skips a company already picked *within the current run* (the in-memory
  `companies` set built up as the run goes). The only cross-run company check,
  [lastSubmissionToCompany](server/src/persistence/application-repository.ts#L110-L118),
  looks solely at when an application was submitted or last attempted — it has
  no idea a company already has an application sitting in `preparing` or
  `review` from a previous run.

## Acceptance criteria

1. At the start of a run, any application in `preparing` for longer than a
   defined staleness threshold (~30 minutes) is moved to `failed`, with a note
   explaining why, before candidates are counted or selected — so it no longer
   counts toward the review-queue count.
2. Each application recovered this way gets an audit entry (a permanent record
   of what changed and who/what changed it) recorded under a non-user actor
   (e.g. `scheduler`), consistent with assisted-apply rule 12.
3. The recovery touches only `preparing` rows older than the threshold. Every
   other status (`review`, `approved`, `previewed`, `submitted`,
   `needs_attention`, `cancelled`, and `preparing` rows still within the
   threshold) is left exactly as it was, and no approval, fill or submit code
   path is ever called.
4. A job whose company already has an application in `preparing` or `review`
   — from any earlier run, not only the current one — is skipped as a
   candidate, the same way a same-run company match is skipped today.
5. The existing per-run same-company skip and the post-submission
   same-company gap (the cool-down period before re-applying to a company you
   already applied to) keep working unchanged alongside the new cross-run
   check in (4).

## Technical notes

- Suggested fix for (1)-(3): at the start of
  [AutoPrepareService.run](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L57-L84),
  before computing the available room, mark `preparing` applications older
  than the threshold as `failed` through `ApplicationRepository`, recording
  the audit entry under `scheduler`. Whether the server's own start-up should
  *also* recover them (mirroring `recoverInterruptedRuns` /
  `RunRepository.markInterrupted`, so a stuck row does not wait for the next
  CLI run) is left as an open question below rather than decided here.
- Suggested fix for (4)-(5): extend
  [AutoPrepareService.skipReason](server/src/services/apply/auto-prepare-service.ts#L110-L120)'s
  company check (or the underlying query) to also treat a company with an
  existing `preparing` or `review` application as a match, alongside the
  current in-run set and the `lastSubmissionToCompany` gap.
- Neither fix changes `application-service.ts`, the `approved → previewed →
  submitted` path, or any assisted-apply guardrail; both stay inside
  `AutoPrepareService` and the application repository.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the approval gate, fill or submit paths, or to
  `application-service.ts`.
- Recovering a run's sweep record — that path (`RunRepository.markInterrupted`)
  already exists and is unaffected.
- Surfacing recovered/skipped applications in the UI beyond what already shows
  a `failed` status and its note.

## Open questions

- Should the server's own start-up also recover stale `preparing`
  applications (mirroring `recoverInterruptedRuns` for sweep runs), or is
  recovery at the start of each `auto-prepare` CLI run enough? Carried from
  the PR #12 QA review's "consider whether" — not settled here.
- Is 30 minutes the right staleness threshold, given the ~8-minute typical
  draft time cited in the PR #12 QA review?
